title: Choir and House
premise: When her twin brother Theo dies in the old Eriksen house, Vera takes his name to settle the estate, only to find every mirror lagging one second behind reality — and in that stolen second, something wearing Theo's face is waiting. The house's mirrors are a ledger: in 1974, their grandmother drowned a girl named Ada and took her inheritance, and the frost creeping through the glass is Ada reclaiming it room by room. Vera must uncover the truth the family buried, return what was taken — the deed, the name, the body never properly mourned — while falling for Ada's grandniece, Ruth, who came seeking justice outside any courtroom. In the end Vera gives back everything, including her own reflection, choosing love and restitution over the house; the frost completes its pattern, the mirrors go dark, and the two women walk out of Choir and House into a morning that finally belongs to no one dead.
about_author: Paloma Vane is the pen name of a former church archivist from coastal Maine who spent a decade cataloguing parish records of unquiet burials. She writes haunted domestic horror about families that mistake property for forgiveness.

chapters.title: The Wrong Twin
chapters.summary: Vera arrives at the Eriksen house under her dead twin Theo's name to handle the burial and estate. POV: Vera. Emotional beat: grief braided with impostor's guilt as she signs documents in a hand that isn't hers.

chapters.title: One Second Late
chapters.summary: Alone in the hall bathroom, Vera notices her mirror reflection lags — a blink arriving after her own. She tests it with a dropped comb; the glass is slow. POV: Vera. Beat: rational denial cracking into dread.

chapters.title: The House Remembers Names
chapters.summary: The solicitor, Ms. Okafor, questions 'Theo' too sharply about family history Vera doesn't know. That night the mirrors show rooms furnished as they were decades ago. POV: Vera. Beat: the cost of the lie tightening.

chapters.title: Ruth at the Gate
chapters.summary: A woman named Ruth appears asking about 'the girl from 1974,' claiming family connection to the house. Vera lies badly; Ruth sees through it but stays anyway. POV: Ruth. Beat: wary attraction kindling between them.

chapters.title: Frost in July
chapters.summary: Fern-frost blooms across the interior windows despite summer heat, forming patterns like sheet music. The house hums at night — a choir with no singers. POV: Vera. Beat: wonder curdling into terror.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: In the attic, Vera finds her grandmother's journals: 1974 entries describing Ada, a ward of the family, and a drowning ruled accidental. POV: Vera via journal excerpts. Beat: horror of inherited guilt.

chapters.title: What the Mirror Keeps
chapters.summary: Ruth reveals her family lore: Ada was her great-aunt, erased from records after coming to the Eriksen house. In the hallway mirror they glimpse a second figure standing behind them. POV: Ruth. Beat: alliance formed in shared fear.

chapters.title: Theo's Face
chapters.summary: The lagging reflections begin showing Theo instead of Vera, mouthing words she can't hear. She stops sleeping, stops eating; duty to the dead twin wars with self-preservation. POV: Vera. Beat: identity unraveling.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Wall
chapters.summary: Behind the parlor wainscoting they find the original 1974 deed — the house signed over to Ada days before she died, then hidden. POV: Ruth. Beat: proof; justice has an address now.

chapters.title: Okafor's Warning
chapters.summary: Ms. Okafor admits she's handled three Eriksen deaths and each time advised selling; the family always refused. She warns Vera: the house keeps what it's given. POV: Okafor. Beat: outside perspective confirming the pattern.

chapters.title: Choir Practice
chapters.summary: The humming resolves into hymns; following it, Vera finds the sealed chapel where Ada sang, and the mirrors there show the drowning in fragments. POV: Vera. Beat: witness — she cannot unknow what she saw.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Ruth and Vera admit their feelings in the frozen garden, knowing the house punishes attachment. They plan to leave together — but the doors now open onto mirrored rooms. POV: Ruth. Beat: tenderness sharpened by entrapment.

chapters.title: The Family Arrives
chapters.summary: Distant cousins descend for the reading of the will, greedy and oblivious, mocking talk of ghosts. The frost spreads to their bedrooms overnight. POV: ensemble/Okafor. Beat: the house begins collecting from everyone.

chapters.title: First Taken
chapters.summary: Cousin Daniel is found inside a mirror's frame, alive but aged, repeating Ada's last words. The survivors flee to the village; the road loops back to the gate. POV: Vera. Beat: escalation — the house is done being subtle.

chapters.title: 1974, Whole
chapters.summary: In the chapel mirror, Vera experiences Ada's final night entire: the grandmother's jealousy over the inheritance, the pond, the held breath. POV: Vera/Ada interwoven. Beat: full knowledge; rage and grief fused.

chapters.title: The Price of Return
chapters.summary: Okafor researches the legal impossibility of posthumous transfer and proposes a ritual alternative recorded in parish archives: restitution witnessed by the living. But it requires a life given to the glass. POV: Okafor. Beat: hope with a terrible invoice.

chapters.title: What Was Taken
chapters.summary: They gather the debts: the deed, Ada's remains from the pauper plot, her name restored to the family Bible, the grandmother's confession read aloud. The mirrors begin clearing — except the chapel's. POV: Ruth. Beat: restitution working, but incomplete.

chapters.title: The Final Pattern
chapters.summary: The frost completes its design across every window: a score. The choir sings openly now, and the house offers a trade — a soul for the door. Theo's reflection pleads with Vera to take it instead. POV: Vera. Beat: temptation of the easy sacrifice.

chapters.title: Choir and House
chapters.summary: At the climax, Vera refuses both trades and instead steps fully into the mirror to face Ada herself — offering not a death but recognition, apology, and her own name surrendered so Ada's can stand. POV: Vera. Beat: love against duty, paid in identity.

chapters.title: The Glass Goes Dark
chapters.summary: Ada accepts. The mirrors still, the frost melts, the choir falls silent mid-note. The house releases everyone; Daniel wakes diminished but alive. POV: Ruth. Beat: release, and the terror of waiting for Vera.

chapters.title: Morning Without Heirs
chapters.summary: Ruth waits at the gate until dawn; Vera emerges changed — her reflection returns slowly, hesitantly, hers again. They sign the house over to a land trust and burn nothing, keeping the truth. POV: Ruth. Beat: quiet joy after horror.

chapters.title: Coda: What the Frost Wrote
chapters.summary: Months later, a plaque names Ada Eriksen in the chapel garden. Vera visits once, leaves flowers, and does not look at any glass on the way home. POV: Vera. Beat: inheritance redefined — memory kept, debt paid, future chosen.
